title: RMM Tool Abuse
overview: Review a remote-support session for a tool absent from the organization’s approved inventory.
prerequisites: Read the baseline and compare event fields. No external tools are required.

attack.name: Remote Desktop Software
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: An external remote-support session using an unapproved tool should be matched to a valid support case.
evidence: Check the tool identity, origin, actor and support authorization. Correlate session and process activity.
false_positive: A current vendor support case may temporarily require a third-party tool.
tuning: Track temporary approvals by publisher, host and time. Remove unused remote tools from the inventory.
response: Verify the support request, terminate unauthorized sessions and review activity performed during the session.
prevention: Allow approved support tools only, require MFA and maintain an inventory of remote-access agents.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The sample records only session metadata. The lab does not open a remote session or bundle a remote-access tool.

questions.prompt: What should explain a legitimate session?
options: An approved support case tied to the tool and host
Any connection from an external IP
questions.explanation: An approved case provides scope, owner and time.

questions.prompt: What helps verify actions during the session?
questions.explanation: Audit evidence can reveal what the operator did.
